messages.author: 91412968a7969648
messages.subject: 4way mapping
parts:
Hi all:

I've been working with an outbred 4-way population in R/qtl.  We took 4 outbred (heterogeneously heterozygous) grandparents and crossed them to make 2 parents, and then crossed them to make a large set of outbred fullsibs. We've resequenced the population and our markers are all fully informative and phased AB x CD.  I've been running scanone in r/qtl for some preliminary mapping. It would be nice if we could do some genomescans that allow control for background residual genetic variation.  However, my understanding is that cim and stepwiseqtl in r/qtl have not been implemented for the 4way design. I'm wondering whether it would be helpful to consider loco scans using r/qtl2.  Has anyone worked with a 4-way in r/qtl2?  I tried to use "convert2cross2" but it is not working for 4way designs.  Any thoughts or suggestions on moving to r/qtl2?  

Best,
Tom

messages.author: 90b86c41c3f69251
messages.subject: RE: [SOCIAL NETWORK] [Rqtl2-disc] 4way mapping
parts:
I forget what the data structures looked like in r/qtl, but scan1() in qtl2 doesn’t require a cross object.  You pass in phenotypes, genoprobs, covariates, kinship, etc.  Can you convert the r/qtl genoprobs into qtl2 format? It might require a bit of bioinformatics, but I think it’s possible. We have a 4 way cross as well, but it’s a back-burner project at the moment…

 

Dan

messages.subject: Re: [SOCIAL NETWORK] [Rqtl2-disc] 4way mapping
parts:
I haven't yet implemented analysis of 4-way crosses in R/qtl2, but it's straightforward how to do so.
Converting the genotype probabilities to the format for R/qtl2, as Dan suggested, is probably your best bet.

stepwiseqtl() in R/qtl should work for 4-way crosses. But yeah, cim() doesn't. But I recommend against cim() in general.

karl

Hi Dan

I'm Taslima, a graduate student from Tom's Lab. I was playing on this 4way cross that Tom described and have converted r/qtl genoprob for r/qtl2 format but when I was running calc_kinship I realize 4way cross is not supported to calculate kinship for r/qtl2.
Any thought?

Here is my code:

datmap<-pull.map(dataIM)
probs <- vector("list", length(datmap))

nmap <- vector("list", length(datmap))

  
n.ind <- nind(data)
chrnames <- chrnames(data)
is_x_chr <- logical(length = length(chrnames))
names(is_x_chr)<-chrnames
alleles<-as.vector(c("A","B","C","D"))

names(probs) <- names(datmap)
attr(probs, "is_x_chr") <- is_x_chr
attr(probs, "crosstype") <- "4way"
attr(probs,"alleles") <-alleles
attr(probs,"alleleprobs")<-logical(1)
attr(probs,"class")<-c("calc_genoprob" ,"list")

for (i in 1:length(probs)) {
  arr<-dataIM$geno[[names(probs)[i]]]$prob
  flat<-adply(arr,2)
  column.names <- c("AC","BC","AD","BD")
  row.names <- rownames(dataIM$pheno)
  matrix.names <- attributes(dataIM$geno[[names(probs)[i]]]$prob)$dimnames[[2]] #gsub("(\\.)[A-z][A-z]","",colnames(test),perl = T)
  dim<-attributes(dataIM$geno[[names(probs)[i]]]$prob)$dim

  narr <- array(unlist(flat[,-1]),dim = c(dim[1],dim[3],dim[2]),dimnames = list(row.names,column.names,matrix.names))
  probs[[names(probs)[i]]]<-narr
  
  nmap[[names(probs)[i]]] <-unlist(as.data.frame(attributes(dataIM$geno[[names(probs)[i]]]$prob)$map)[1,])

}

attr(probs, "map") <- nmap

kinship <- calc_kinship(probs)

And the error is:

Error in .genoprob_to_alleleprob(attr(probs, "crosstype"), aperm(probs[[chr]],  : 
  cross type not yet supported.

Best,
Taslima

parts:
Hi Karl

I have few more queries for this 4-way cross issue:

1. The plant we are working on is a tetraploid therefore to match multiple sets of chromosomes we marked chromosomes as 1N, 1K, 2N, 2K, which makes each chr  as string, not numeric. So, when I'm going to plot the result of scanone in rqtl2 I got the following error

"Error in plot.window(...) : need finite 'xlim' values"

Do you thing changing the chr names into numerics will help? something like this :

chrnames <- seq(1:18) 

In that case do you thing I need to change marker names too?

2. I also tried find_peaks and then I realize the way I converted genotype probability rqtl2 can not distinguish between pseudomarker and real marker. There are multiple pseudomarkers as loc.xx which may present for all 18 chr so I'm getting the following error:

Error in `levels<-`(`*tmp*`, value = if (nl == nL) as.character(labels) else paste0(labels,  : 
  factor level [2] is duplicated

Do you think I should change the name of these pseudomarkers according to their chr?


Here, I'm attaching my cross object which is "dataIM" and following is my code to convert  data for rqtl2 and run scanone:

https://drive.google.com/open?id=1mnbW6rU8on3MvyThy-_ogmYuOBY_GV1v

datmap<-pull.map(dataIM)
probs <- vector("list", length(datmap))

nmap <- vector("list", length(datmap))

n.ind <- nind(dataIM)
chrnames <- chrnames(dataIM)

is_x_chr <- logical(length = length(chrnames))
names(is_x_chr)<-chrnames
alleles<-as.vector(c("A","B","C","D"))

names(probs) <- names(datmap)
attr(probs, "is_x_chr") <- is_x_chr
attr(probs, "crosstype") <- "4way"
attr(probs,"alleles") <-alleles
attr(probs,"alleleprobs")<-logical(1)
attr(probs,"class")<-c("calc_genoprob" ,"list")

for (i in 1:length(probs)) {
  arr<-dataIM$geno[[names(probs)[i]]]$prob
  flat<-adply(arr,2)
  column.names <- c("AC","BC","AD","BD")
  row.names <- rownames(dataIM$pheno)
  matrix.names <- attributes(dataIM$geno[[names(probs)[i]]]$prob)$dimnames[[2]] #gsub("(\\.)[A-z][A-z]","",colnames(test),perl = T)
  dim<-attributes(dataIM$geno[[names(probs)[i]]]$prob)$dim

  narr <- array(unlist(flat[,-1]),dim = c(dim[1],dim[3],dim[2]),dimnames = list(row.names,column.names,matrix.names))
  probs[[names(probs)[i]]]<-narr
  
  nmap[[names(probs)[i]]] <-unlist(as.data.frame(attributes(dataIM$geno[[names(probs)[i]]]$prob)$map)[1,])

}


attr(probs, "map") <- nmap

kinship <- calc_kinship(probs,use_allele_probs = F)
kinship_loco <- calc_kinship(probs,use_allele_probs = F,type = "loco")

pheno<-as.matrix(dataIM$pheno[,-3])
rownames(pheno)<-rownames(dataIM$pheno)

out<-scan1(probs, pheno ,kinship = kinship_loco)
out_perm<-scan1perm(probs, pheno ,kinship = kinship_loco,cores = 3,n_perm = 100)
summary(out_perm,alpha = 0.05)

find_peaks(out,threshold = 4.99,map = nmap)


Best,
Taslima

parts:
> On Aug 13, 2018, at 3:38 PM, taslima haque <tah...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> Hi Karl
>
> I have few more queries for this 4-way cross issue:
>
> 1. The plant we are working on is a tetraploid therefore to match multiple sets of chromosomes we marked chromosomes as 1N, 1K, 2N, 2K, which makes each chr as string, not numeric. So, when I'm going to plot the result of scanone in rqtl2 I got the following error
>
> "Error in plot.window(...) : need finite 'xlim' values"
>
> Do you thing changing the chr names into numerics will help? something like this :
>
> chrnames <- seq(1:18)
>
> In that case do you thing I need to change marker names too?
>

The chromosome names are stored as character strings not integers, so I don't think this is the cause of the problem.
They're actually taken from the names of the components of the map object.

My guess is that you've got some NAs for marker positions in the map?

> 2. I also tried find_peaks and then I realize the way I converted genotype probability rqtl2 can not distinguish between pseudomarker and real marker. There are multiple pseudomarkers as loc.xx which may present for all 18 chr so I'm getting the following error:
>
> Error in `levels<-`(`*tmp*`, value = if (nl == nL) as.character(labels) else paste0(labels, :
> factor level [2] is duplicated
>
>
> Do you think I should change the name of these pseudomarkers according to their chr?
>

Yes, I would make sure that all pseudomarkers have unique names. They end up as rownames in the output of scan1() and so need to be distinct.

karl

This seems like a case where one or more of the possible genotypes are not observed, and so some estimated coefficients become unestimable.

I don’t have great solutions to this at present, but you can try using clean_genoprob() to set small values of the genotype probabilities to 0.

karl

The chromosome names are stored as character strings not integers, so I don't think this is the cause of the problem.
They're actually taken from the names of the components of the map object.

My guess is that you've got some NAs for marker positions in the map?


> 2. I also tried find_peaks and then I realize the way I converted genotype probability rqtl2 can not distinguish between pseudomarker and real marker. There are multiple pseudomarkers as loc.xx which may present for all 18 chr so I'm getting the following error:

>
>

>

Yes, I would make sure that all pseudomarkers have unique names. They end up as rownames in the output of scan1() and so need to be distinct.

karl

Thanks for the reply.

We tried the way you suggested as masking small probability as 0s, it still did not solve the problem.

The University of Texas, Austin

From: Karl Broman
Sent: Thursday, March 28, 2019 8:54 AM
To: rqtl2...@googlegroups.com

This seems like a case where one or more of the possible genotypes are not observed, and so some estimated coefficients become unestimable.

 

I don’t have great solutions to this at present, but you can try using clean_genoprob() to set small values of the genotype probabilities to 0.

 

karl

messages.subject: RE: [Rqtl2-disc] 4way mapping
parts:
The problems with unstable coefficient estimates will not be easily solved and likely has no general solution. Except with very large populations, there are likely to be regions of some chromosomes that give crazy coefficient estimates.

I’d recommend maybe just focusing on estimates at particular QTL positions, with plot_pxg() or fit1().

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl2-disc] 4way mapping
parts:
Hi Li,

Please could you tell more about the bug you found in your code? Because I got the same issue with extremely large QTL effect for HS rats population, and hopefully with your hint, I can solve it. Many thanks!

Best wishes,
Thu
On 1 Apr 2019, at 18:03, Li Zhang <zhang...@gmail.com> wrote:

Hi Karl,
We re-checked anything in our script, it turns out to be a bug in our code. Now the QTL effects seems normal.
One more quick question, is there an easy way to plot effect and se together in the same map using plot_coef? Or I need to extract the data from effect and SE separately, and probably customized it.
Thanks
 
Li Zhang, Ph.D
Postdoctoral Fellow
 
 
 
From: Karl Broman
Sent: Friday, March 29, 2019 10:30 AM
To: R/qtl2 discussion
Subject: RE: [Rqtl2-disc] 4way mapping
 
The problems with unstable coefficient estimates will not be easily solved and likely has no general solution. Except with very large populations, there are likely to be regions of some chromosomes that give crazy coefficient estimates.
 
I’d recommend maybe just focusing on estimates at particular QTL positions, with plot_pxg() or fit1().
 
karl

Our bug was about the formatting  when changing calculated probabilities from R/qtl1 to qtl2, which doesn’t deal with 4way population at the moment. So I am not sure I can help. 
However, Karl mentioned you might want to try changing the small probabilities into 0s using clean_prob.


-Li
